{"task":{"id":"Prob093_ece241_2014_q3","spec":"
I would like you to implement a module named TopModule with the following
interface. All input and output ports are one bit unless otherwise
specified.

 - input  c
 - input  d
 - output mux_in (4 bits)

For the following Karnaugh map, give the circuit implementation using one
4-to-1 multiplexer and as many 2-to-1 multiplexers as required, but using
as few as possible. You are not allowed to use any other logic gate and
you must use _a_ and _b_ as the multiplexer selector inputs, as shown on
the 4-to-1 multiplexer below.

      ab
  cd  00  01  11  10
  00 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 |
  01 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  11 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 |
  10 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 |

Consider a block diagram with inputs 'c' and 'd' going into a module
called "TopModule". This "TopModule" has four outputs, mux_in[3:0], that
connect to a four input mux. The mux takes as input {a,b} and ab = 00 is
connected to mux_in[0], ab=01 is connected to mux_in[1], and so in. You
are implementing in Verilog just the portion labelled "TopModule", such
that the entire circuit (including the 4-to-1 mux) implements the K-map.

","interface":{"top":"TopModule","ports":[{"name":"c","direction":"input","width":1,"signed":false},{"name":"d","direction":"input","width":1,"signed":false},{"name":"mux_in","direction":"output","width":4,"signed":false}]},"constraints":"SystemVerilog, exactly one self-contained TopModule DUT. Inline all helper logic inside TopModule; do not define auxiliary modules. xczu3eg-sbva484-1-e; 5 ns synthesis clock; simulator seed 1. No reference dependencies, hierarchy outside the DUT, file access, includes or DPI."},"current":{"revision_id":"6abf6c97-f184-485a-94ed-f9bab058ac30","source_sha256":"0f889e18feb2ed996b9661687048b483039c20b55b22ab84e795881bbae30463","source":"module TopModule (
    input c,
    input d,
    output [3:0] mux_in
);
    // K-map columns selected by ab:
    // ab=00 -> mux_in[0], ab=01 -> mux_in[1], ab=11 -> mux_in[2], ab=10 -> mux_in[3]
    // cd rows: {00,01,11,10}
    assign mux_in[0] = c | d;     // {0,1,1,1}
    assign mux_in[1] = 1'b0;      // {0,0,0,0}
    assign mux_in[2] = c & d;     // {0,0,1,0}
    assign mux_in[3] = c | ~d;    // {1,0,1,1}
endmodule
